summary: The smallest unbounded and dominating families of natural-number functions obey cardinal and cofinality bounds.
abstract: Given countably many functions from the natural numbers to themselves, one can find a single function that exceeds each of them at all sufficiently large inputs. How many functions are needed before no common eventual bound exists? The bounding number answers this question, while the dominating number answers a complementary one: how many functions suffice so that every function is eventually bounded by one of them? Both sizes are uncountable and at most the size of the real line, and the bounding number is no larger than the dominating number.
